Yol.Y: In the near future a process of growth may take shape in which you redefine yourself and prepare more firmly for new beginnings.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you turn the ruptures of the past into part of your growth and move towards a new direction in life of your own choosing.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to accept the new self formed after change and to build your future independent of the limits of the past.

S4-K1.dAnlam: When the Moonlight Stag comes upright, it reminds you that as you move along an uncertain path, you can draw support from your intuition and from the quiet signs around you. The sacred stag appearing beneath three crescents symbolises that not every answer is spoken aloud; sometimes the right direction can be felt through a calm awareness that comes from within. You too may begin to understand your own needs better in a matter you have long been undecided about. This card stresses the importance of connecting with nature, listening to trustworthy guides and making room for your inner voice. Now you can seek your path not with fear but with careful observation and intuitive trust, and choose your next steps more consciously.
S4-K1.yAnlam: When the Moonlight Stag comes sideways, the sacred stag has not yet stepped out of the depths of the forest; it waits, among the changing phases of moonlight, for the traveller to sense their own direction. You too may be trying to understand which signs to trust in your life, finding it hard to tell your intuition from your worries. This card advises you to listen to the silence of your inner world rather than trying to resolve uncertainty at once. Sometimes, before guidance can come from outside, a person must be ready to accept it. When you give your feelings time, notice the trustworthy support around you and avoid hasty decisions, the first lines of a path that seems dark can begin to appear.
S4-K1.hikaye: In the first nights of the realm of spirits, a mysterious stag lived among the roots of four ancient intertwined trees, lighting lost paths; its antlers gathered moonlight, and its steps awakened memories hidden deep in the earth. One night a traveller who had lost his way saw the stag's pale light in the darkness of the forest, and as he began to follow it, he heard among the whispers of the trees forgotten voices from his own past. The stag did not tell him which road to choose; it only stood beneath three crescents and waited for him to notice the direction his heart had heard. From that day on, the Moonlight Stag became a sacred symbol reminding us that when a person listens to their own intuition, they can find guidance in the quiet signs of nature.
S4-K1.mitDers: In the Dreaming traditions the land carries the traces of ancestral journeys; the way is found by reading the signs of nature. The stag is not native to Australia; it is the card's own original guide.
S4-K1.mitDikkat: Handing your intuition over to outside approval, or reading the signs in haste.
S4-K1.mitGercek: The card's main inspiration comes from the way, in these traditions, the journeys of ancestral beings shaped the earth, natural features took on meaning, and people formed a spiritual bond with the lands they live on. Dreaming narratives are not the same in all Aboriginal communities; they differ according to particular lands, languages and cultural traditions. Deer are also not native animals of Australia; they were brought to the continent after European settlement.

Kök.D: A direction you found in the past by trusting your intuition, or with the support of a trustworthy guide, may have formed the basis of your inner confidence today.
Kök.Y: An intuitive awareness you did not take seriously in the past, or support you quietly received, may be waiting to take on new meaning today.

Şimdi.D: Right now you can combine your intuition with careful observation and set a surer direction for yourself in an uncertain matter.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to tell your inner voice from your worries and need to understand your feelings before you decide.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to choose your own direction consciously, without letting trust in your intuition turn into ignoring the facts.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to weigh your inner signs patiently, without confusing the sensitivity you feel in uncertainty with fear.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your intuitive sensitivity, your bond with nature and your ability to accept trustworthy guidance when needed.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to observe quietly, to listen to your feelings and your openness to discovering your own inner direction.

Yol.D: In the near future an encounter that catches your attention, or a new awareness, may help you weigh the options before you more clearly.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by making sense of the uncertainties in your inner world, you may discover more calmly which way you want to go.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you trust your own intuition, notice the support around you and choose your life's path more consciously.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to learn the language of your inner guidance and to build self-trust even amid uncertainty.

S4-K2.dAnlam: When the Winged River's Memory comes upright, it reminds you that an experience from your past may give you new meaning today. The two linked loops of the infinity sign symbolise that memories are not only events left behind; they carry an unseen current that feeds your thoughts and choices today. You too may recall a piece of knowledge, a word or an experience you thought you had long forgotten. This card stresses the importance of sharing the valuable traces of the past and passing on what you have learned to others. Now you can look at your own story with different eyes and carry into your future the wisdom distilled from what you have lived. As the river flows, memories change shape, but the meaning they carry is never wholly lost.
S4-K2.yAnlam: When the Winged River's Memory comes sideways, the river has not yet spread its wings; it keeps the memories it carries from the past in its own depths. You too may be trying to understand why certain memories keep returning to your mind, or why something you heard in the past feels different today. This card reminds you that not every memory needs to be explained or shared at once. Some experiences take on their true meaning only as time passes. When you weigh the memories moving through your inner world without judging them, you can notice which pieces of knowledge strengthen you and which now call for a different reading. The river's quiet flow asks you to absorb the wisdom of the past before carrying it into the future.
S4-K2.hikaye: In the first ages of the realm of spirits, a mysterious river born among the roots of intertwined ancient trees gathered in its waters the voices forgotten on earth, the words never spoken and the memories of the past that were fading away. One day, when its path was cut off by a great rock, an unseen power that would not let its memories be lost gave it wings of water, and the river left its bed and carried its memories to distant lands that only the wind could reach. Wherever the river passed, people noticed the feelings stirred in them by old stories they had never heard, and began to understand the invisible bonds between past and present. From that day on, the Winged River's Memory became a sacred sign reminding us that what has been lived is never wholly lost, and that memories, passed on in different forms, can become the wisdom of new lives.
S4-K2.mitDers: A songline carries a route, and the knowledge of that route, from generation to generation in song; memory is not a static archive but a road that is walked.
S4-K2.mitDikkat: Either rejecting the past entirely or living inside it.
S4-K2.mitGercek: In some of these traditions, the journeys of ancestral beings are associated with the forming of rivers, water sources and landforms; the knowledge of these journeys is preserved through stories, songs and cultural narratives handed down through the generations. In particular, the ancestral routes known as songlines, which link geographical places while also carrying knowledge from the past, inspire the card's theme of memory and continuity.

Kök.D: An important experience, piece of advice or family story passed down to you may have formed the basis of the values that shape your life today.
Kök.Y: A memory you could not fully make sense of in the past, or something you once heard, may be waiting to take on new meaning in your inner world today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by recalling what your past experiences have taught you, you can give your present choices a deeper meaning.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to understand how the memories resurfacing in your mind connect with what you feel today.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to keep the valuable knowledge of the past without letting old experiences alone determine your life today.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to weigh patiently the meanings that memories from the past awaken in you today, without interpreting them in haste.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your memory, what you have learned from past experience and your ability to share valuable knowledge with others.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to sense the meanings within your memories and to quietly reconsider your past experiences.

Yol.D: In the near future something you recall from the past, or a renewed connection, may help you weigh the options before you differently.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by better grasping the meaning of an old experience, you may bring clarity to thoughts that are not yet complete.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you keep the wisdom of the past, pass your own experience on to others and form meaningful links between the different periods of your life.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to discover the deeper meaning of your memories and to use what you have learned from the past more consciously in the future.

S4-K3.dAnlam: When Whisper of the Roots comes upright, a period appears in which you can see more clearly the value of the unseen bonds that keep you standing. Roots reaching deep into the earth remind you that your strength is fed not only by your own efforts, but also by the surroundings you belong to, your relationships and the values that come from the past. You too may come to appreciate anew a support you have long overlooked, or a commitment that gives your life meaning. This card advises you to honour your roots without losing your independence. Now you can strengthen the relationships that nourish you and build a firmer, more conscious bond between your own being and the life around you.
S4-K3.yAnlam: When Whisper of the Roots comes sideways, the roots of the ancient tree have not yet fully reached one another; they are still searching for the unseen connections deep in the soil. You too may be questioning where you feel you belong, which values truly nourish you, or what place the ties you carry from your past have in your life today. This card does not ask you to build a strong sense of belonging at once, but to come to know patiently the relationships and experiences that have shaped you. Sometimes a person notices their roots only when they feel they have drifted away from them. When you give your inner questions time, you can see more clearly which bonds you want to keep and which you want to understand anew.
S4-K3.hikaye: In the ancient ages of the realm of spirits, the roots of trees reaching in four directions joined one another in the unseen depths of the soil, and each tree felt the life of the whole forest beyond its own leaves. One day a young tree that wanted to grow alone decided to separate its roots from the others; then it heard a mysterious whisper rising from the earth and learned that the strength that nourished it came not only from its own trunk but from countless unseen relationships around it. When the tree reached its roots back into the depths of the soil, four sacred stags appeared around it, and an invisible eye opened among its branches so that it could see the bonds of life hidden beneath the ground. From that day on, Whisper of the Roots became a sacred sign reminding us that a person draws strength not only from their own being, but from the land they belong to, the relationships they form and the bonds that stretch from the past to the present.
S4-K3.mitDers: In the concept of Country, a person belongs to the land as much as they are responsible for it; roots bring obligations as well as rights.
S4-K3.mitDikkat: Turning belonging into dependence or pressure.
S4-K3.mitGercek: In these traditions, the relationships of ancestral beings with the earth are linked to the spiritual meanings of lands, plants, animals and natural features. In Aboriginal cultures, the concept of Country covers not only a geographical area but the cultural and spiritual relationships between people, ancestors, living beings and the land they live on. Oral narratives and knowledge of ancestral routes handed down over generations help people keep their bond with the place they live and understand their responsibilities towards it.

Kök.D: The support you received from your family, the surroundings you grew up in or strong relationships you formed may have laid the foundation of the resilience you have today.
Kök.Y: A sense of belonging you could not fully understand in the past, or a question about your origins, may be feeding your need today to know yourself better.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by noticing the relationships that nourish you and the values that give your life meaning, you can develop a firmer sense of belonging.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to understand with which people, places and values you have a genuine bond.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to keep the valuable bonds that come from the past while maintaining your individuality and independent choices.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to discover the meaning of your own roots without letting the wish to belong turn into giving in to others' expectations.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your trustworthy relationships, the values you gained from the past and the mutual commitment you share with the life around you.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to question your own origins and to tell apart the bonds that truly nourish you.

Yol.D: In the near future a chance may arise to strengthen the valuable relationships in your life and create surroundings where you feel more at home.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by reassessing some values that come from your past, you may understand which bonds you want to strengthen in your life.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you draw strength from your roots, keep your mutual bond with those around you and build a firm sense of belonging in your own life.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to know your origins more deeply and to understand the bonds of the past anew in line with your own values.

mitFigur: Knowledge carried by the wind (in some communities)
S4-K4.dAnlam: When the Tree the Wind Forgot comes upright, you may recall your own worth in an area where you have long felt unnoticed or felt your voice was not heard enough. The three vertical lines symbolise the tree that goes on standing on its roots even when the movement around it has stopped. You too may begin to see the abilities you have without waiting for others' attention, appreciation or support. This card reminds you that being forgotten does not mean being worthless. Now you can take steps to express yourself, revive a side of you that you have neglected, and consciously create the place you deserve in your life. Even if your voice is not heard, your presence goes on carrying meaning.
S4-K4.yAnlam: When the Tree the Wind Forgot comes sideways, the old tree has not yet discovered the voice rising from its own roots; it waits in silence for the wind to return one day. You too may feel that you are not seen enough in your life, that your efforts go unnoticed, or that a bond in which you once felt strong has weakened. This card advises you that you do not have to keep trying harder to remind others of yourself. Sometimes a feeling of loneliness can create a chance to redefine within yourself the worth you expect from others. When you understand the needs within the silence, you can discover which relationships nourish you and how to make more room for your own being.
S4-K4.hikaye: In the ancient forests of the realm of spirits, as the wind touched the branches of every tree and carried its voice to distant lands, it forgot to pass by an old tree at the edge of the forest, and over time the tree sank into a deep silence in which not even its own whisper could be heard. At first the tree waited for the wind to come back, but as the seasons passed it noticed its leaves falling and its branches growing quiet, while the spark of life it kept beneath the soil still lived on. One night, listening to the voices of the trees around it in the moonlight, it heard for the first time a fine vibration rising from its own roots, and understood that it did not have to wait for the wind to touch it again in order to be remembered. From that day on, the Tree the Wind Forgot became the sacred sign of keeping one's presence without being lost in oblivion, of building a self-worth independent of the world's attention, and of finding one's own voice again within silence.
S4-K4.mitDers: In Dreaming thought, a place's worth comes not from being seen but from the story it carries; being forgotten is not the same as being worthless.
S4-K4.mitDikkat: Making your own worth depend on others remembering you.
S4-K4.mitGercek: In these traditions, the relationships between land, trees, wind, living beings and ancestral beings are bound up with the spiritual and cultural meaning of the place where people live; the concept of Country covers not only a person's presence in a landscape but the relationships of mutual belonging and responsibility they form with it.

Kök.D: Keeping your strength during a time when you were not noticed enough may have formed the basis of the self-worth you have today.
Kök.Y: An experience in which you felt your voice was not heard may be affecting your need today to be seen and accepted.

Şimdi.D: Right now you can remember your own worth without waiting for others' appreciation, and bring forward a side of yourself you have long kept in the background.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may feel insufficiently understood and be trying to grasp how this feeling relates to your sense of your own worth.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to keep the value of your own presence without making your wish to be visible depend on others' approval.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to understand your inner needs with compassion, without reading a sense of loneliness or being forgotten as personal worthlessness.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your inner resilience, your skill at recognising your own values and your ability to keep growing independent of others' attention.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to listen to yourself in silence and to grow within yourself first the acceptance you expect from outside.

Yol.D: In the near future, by expressing again a talent or idea you have long neglected, you may open a new space of visibility for yourself.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by understanding in which settings you can express yourself more freely, you may prepare for new steps that strengthen your own voice.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you know the worth of your own presence without needing others to remember you, and can create a place of your own in life.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to recognise the needs behind the feeling of being forgotten and to develop your inner strength independently of others' approval.

S4-K5.dAnlam: When the Petrified Flower Garden comes upright, you can develop a new understanding between your wish to preserve a beauty you once valued and the natural change of life. The three rings that cross and link with one another symbolise that moments once lived can endure in different layers of meaning without being lost. You too may notice what place a memory, relationship or achievement you have long kept holds in your life today. This card advises you to preserve the value of the past without letting it leave you motionless. Now you can keep beautiful memories alive not in their unchanging forms but through the meaning they have given you, and make room for new beauty as well.
S4-K5.yAnlam: When the Petrified Flower Garden comes sideways, the garden's keeper has not yet turned the flowers to stone, but fearing they might wither, wishes to stop the flow of time. You too may be wary of a period, relationship or beautiful experience you value greatly changing. This card does not suggest rejecting your attachment to the past, but understanding why you want to preserve it exactly as it is. Sometimes the fear of loss can make it harder to open up to new experiences. When you accept the value of your memories while seeing change as a natural part of life, you can allow the beauty you wish to preserve to live within you without limiting you.
S4-K5.hikaye: In the first springs of the realm of spirits, there was a mysterious flower garden blooming among four ancient trees, and its flowers took on different colours every season, celebrating nature's passing beauty. One day the garden's keeper, afraid that the flowers would wither and vanish, placed three invisible rings around them, and all the flowers turned to stone at their most beautiful moment, sheltered from the touch of time. Years later a traveller who came to the garden saw that the petrified flowers were still enchanting but could no longer dance with the wind, and understood the difference between preserving beauty and stopping the flow of life. From that day on, the Petrified Flower Garden became a sacred sign reminding us that while we preserve the precious beauties of the past, we must also allow them to change, and that true permanence lies not in form but in the meaning left behind.
S4-K5.mitDers: In some accounts the traces of ancestral beings become permanent in rocks and water sources; what is precious is preserved not by freezing but by changing form.
S4-K5.mitDikkat: Freezing beauty and stopping the flow of life.
S4-K5.mitGercek: In some of these traditions, the earth was shaped during the journeys of ancestral beings, and their traces live on in rocks, trees, water sources and other natural features; this inspires the card's idea of a living being turning into a lasting form of nature. In some Dreaming narratives presented by the National Museum of Australia, the idea that natural features carry the traces and spiritual presence of ancestral beings holds an important place. Aboriginal peoples, however, do not have a single shared mythology; the narratives differ according to particular communities, languages and lands.

Kök.D: Being able to preserve a memory or experience you valued in the past may have laid the foundation for noticing the lasting beauties in your life today.
Kök.Y: A beautiful period you did not want to end may be affecting the hesitation you feel towards change today.

Şimdi.D: Right now you can develop a more mature view in which you keep the valuable traces of the past while also making room for new experiences.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to understand why a situation you do not want to change matters so much to you.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to adapt to life's changing conditions while keeping your beautiful memories, and not to place the past before the present.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to not let the fear of losing what you value turn into a clinging that blocks its natural growth.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is what you have learned from the beauties of the past and your ability to keep valuable experiences alive in meaningful ways under new conditions.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to understand your emotional attachments and your skill at showing yourself patience in the face of change.

Yol.D: In the near future, by adapting an experience you valued in the past to new conditions, you may carry its meaning on in your life.
Yol.Y: In the near future you may better understand which aspects of a bond or habit you want to preserve could be open to change.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you can preserve the beauties of the past while still allowing life to bloom with new flowers.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to understand the attachments behind your fear of change, and to keep the lasting meaning of beautiful things alive by accepting their passing forms.

S4-K6.ad: The Rock That Speaks with Rain
mitFigur: The Rainbow Serpent (Kakadu and some communities)
S4-K6.dAnlam: When the Rock That Speaks with Rain comes upright, you may notice that a situation which has long stood unchanged is beginning to take on new meaning through small but steady influences. The lines curling into one another symbolise that even if no single experience changes you at once, over time each can leave lasting traces in your thinking. This card reminds you that being strong does not mean staying rigid in every circumstance. You too may approach the words of people around you, different experiences or the new perspectives life offers with more openness. Now you can turn your patience from a passive wait into a conscious power of learning, and discover that you can keep your essence while you change.
S4-K6.yAnlam: When the Rock That Speaks with Rain comes sideways, the first drops of rain have reached the surface of the rock but have not yet left clear marks. You too may be trying to understand what the small, repeating experiences in your life or the words you hear are trying to tell you. This card reminds you that you do not have to change at once or make firm decisions. Sometimes an idea needs to be heard again at different times before it can ripen. When you listen quietly, observe your reactions and weigh the new information that reaches you, some hardened ideas in your inner world may begin to soften. What the rain teaches gains meaning to the extent that the rock is ready to receive it.
S4-K6.hikaye: In the ancient ages of the realm of spirits, an old rock standing near the roots of four sacred trees had watched the changing colours of the sky for thousands of seasons, but because it had never left its place, it believed it could never learn the stories of the world. One day a long rain began, and with each drop it left on the rock's surface voices carried from distant lands, and the rock discovered that it could communicate with other beings without breaking its silence. These conversations, lasting through the seasons, formed three fine curling traces on the rock; it was now a little different from its old form, yet every change had given it a new understanding. From that day on, the Rock That Speaks with Rain became the sacred sign reminding us that patience is not only waiting, but staying open to the small and constant touches of life and growing a deep wisdom over time.
S4-K6.mitDers: In some accounts the Rainbow Serpent shapes waterways and rocks; form arises through patient and constant contact.
S4-K6.mitDikkat: Confusing patience with being closed to change.
S4-K6.mitGercek: Some of these traditions tell how rocky outcrops, water sources, rivers and other natural features were shaped by the journeys of ancestral beings; these places are bound up with the stories that describe them and with the spiritual relationships formed with the land. In some local narratives of the Kakadu region of Australia, the ancestral being rendered in English as the Rainbow Serpent is associated with water sources and features of the land; the name, qualities and stories of this figure, however, vary between communities.

Kök.D: Repeated experiences you met with patience in the past may have laid the foundation for approaching events with more understanding and maturity today.
Kök.Y: Small experiences or advice you did not weigh enough in the past may be waiting to take on new meaning today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by carefully weighing different ideas from those around you, you can approach a long-unchanged matter more flexibly.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to discover the meaning of the small developments you are living through and need to absorb them before you decide.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to let new experiences help you grow, without turning your resilience into rigidity.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to be patient with a learning process that takes time, without giving in to the wish for quick results.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your patience, your ability to accept different views and to learn from experience slowly but lastingly.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to listen quietly, to give your thoughts time and to notice the value of small changes.

Yol.D: In the near future small, repeating developments may help you form a more mature understanding of a matter you have long seen the same way.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by absorbing new experiences, you may understand which of your ideas are beginning to change and where you need patience.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you learn from life's small touches, join resilience with understanding and meet change with patience.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to grasp the meaning of your experiences over time and to develop your inner transformation without hurrying.

S5-K1.dAnlam: When the Prophecy of the Iron Chain comes upright, you can see more clearly how a promise you made in the past, a responsibility you took on or a commitment you keep is shaping your choices today. The black chains winding around each other remind you that not every bond carries the same meaning. Some give you security and continuity, while others may now ask to be reassessed. This card does not advise you to free yourself from all your ties, but to understand which ones you keep consciously. Now you can set the limits of your responsibilities and weigh the relationships you built in the past more fairly. True freedom is not breaking every chain, but knowing which bonds you carry by your own will.
S5-K1.yAnlam: When the Prophecy of the Iron Chain comes sideways, the guardian of the underworld has not yet decoded the meaning of the chains; he is carefully examining the tangled bonds around the red seal. You too may be questioning why you keep certain responsibilities in your life, or how valid the promises you made in the past still are today. This card asks you to understand from which needs and choices your commitments arose, rather than changing them at once. Sometimes a duty that has become habit can look like a responsibility truly chosen. When you give yourself time, you can tell more clearly the bonds that support you from the obligations you feel narrow your room to move. Learning the meaning of the chains is the first step to carrying them consciously.
S5-K1.hikaye: In the dark passages of the Duat, a nameless guardian charged with protecting Ra's night journey discovered a mysterious chamber where invisible chains were kept, forged from the promises people had made in the past and the responsibilities they had left unfinished. The red seal at the centre of the chamber showed that every chain carried two different meanings; some bonds protected a person, while others, once the reason for them was forgotten, limited their journey. Instead of breaking the chains at random, the guardian chose to understand from which promise each had been born, and created a sacred sign that separated true responsibilities from commitments that had lost their meaning. From that day on, the Prophecy of the Iron Chain became the underworld sign reminding us to notice how the bonds formed in the past can shape our future, and to choose consciously the responsibilities we must carry on the way to freedom.
S5-K1.mitDers: In the Book of Gates, the chaining of Apep protects the cosmic order; a bond is not always captivity, it can also be the restraint of a dangerous power.
S5-K1.mitDikkat: Mistaking commitments kept out of guilt for responsibility.
S5-K1.mitGercek: The card's main mythological source is the passage of the sun god Ra through the otherworld realm called the Duat during the night, and his encounter on this journey with Apep, or Apophis, the serpent who threatens cosmic order. In the eleventh hour of the ancient Egyptian underworld text known as the Book of Gates, Apep is shown rendered powerless with bonds and chains; this scene shows that binding can mean not only captivity but also the restraint of a dangerous power. The gates, guardians and sacred words to be spoken in the tradition of the Book of the Dead also stress the importance of knowledge and responsibility on a person's journey.

Kök.D: An important promise you made or responsibility you took on in the past may have formed the basis of the commitments and choices in your life today.
Kök.Y: An obligation you never fully questioned why you accepted may be shaping your choices today without your noticing.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by weighing more clearly the responsibilities that come from the past, you can decide which bonds you want to keep consciously.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to understand why some of your commitments continue and to discover the real limits of your responsibilities.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to keep your own will and personal limits while owning your responsibilities, without taking on more than you should.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to decode the meaning of your commitments without hasty decisions, while separating your habits from your real obligations.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your past experience, the care you give to your word and your ability to manage your responsibilities consciously.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your patient questioning, your ability to notice your own limits and your skill at tracing the source of your commitments.

Yol.D: In the near future, by rearranging a responsibility you have long carried, you may create a more balanced and sustainable path.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by reassessing the meaning of an obligation from the past, you may better understand on what terms you want to continue.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you take responsibility for the bonds you formed in the past while also keeping your freedom of choice.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to understand the hold of old promises and habits and to redefine your commitments more consciously.

S5-K2.dAnlam: When the Heart of the Black Labyrinth comes upright, it shows that you can draw near to the centre of feelings you have long struggled to make sense of and thoughts that keep repeating. The spiral curling inward reminds you that while you keep looking for the way out in outer conditions, you may have missed an important truth in your own inner world. You too may notice why you give the same reactions in similar situations, or why you keep away from certain feelings. This card advises you to make sense of your inner turmoil without judging yourself. Now you can approach the questions you have avoided more openly and discover the links between your past experiences and your present choices. The centre of the labyrinth may be the beginning of the way out.
S5-K2.yAnlam: When the Heart of the Black Labyrinth comes sideways, the traveller has not yet reached the centre of the labyrinth; among passages that look alike, they are trying to understand which path is their own. You too may be finding it hard to get your bearings among repeating thoughts or emotional reactions you cannot explain. This card does not ask you to find every answer at once, but to observe your inner world patiently. Sometimes returning to the same question again and again can be the sign of a need not yet understood. When you look into the source of your feelings and ask yourself honest questions, the labyrinth's tangled paths can slowly begin to make sense. Before reaching the centre, you must come to know the way.
S5-K2.hikaye: In the dark passages of the Duat, a mysterious labyrinth would sometimes appear before travellers seeking to reach the presence of Osiris, a labyrinth with no stone walls, made only of their own thoughts. Those who entered it noticed that, circling around the fears they had hidden in the past, the reckonings they had postponed and the truths they could not tell themselves, they kept arriving at the same paths again and again. One day a nameless traveller stopped searching for the exit and turned towards the red light at the centre of the labyrinth, and there, instead of a door, found the voice of their own heart that they had long avoided hearing. From that day on, the Heart of the Black Labyrinth became a sacred sign reminding us that the way out of darkness does not always begin by moving outward, but by understanding the tangled paths of one's own inner world and facing the feelings one has hidden.
S5-K2.mitDers: In the Book of Two Ways the soul passes only by knowing the names of the gates and their guardians; the way out of the labyrinth runs through knowledge.
S5-K2.mitDikkat: Turning self-questioning into an endless loop of thought.
S5-K2.mitGercek: The Book of Two Ways, found among the ancient Egyptian Coffin Texts, is the card's main source, as it depicts the different paths, gates and guardians that a soul moving through the underworld may meet. In these texts, two routes stretching over land and water show that the journey consists not only of moving forward but of recognising the obstacles one meets and gaining the knowledge one needs. The confrontation with one's own deeds on the otherworld journey associated with Osiris also inspires the theme of discovering inner truth.

Kök.D: Understanding a feeling you avoided facing in the past may let you see more clearly the source of some behaviour that repeats today.
Kök.Y: An experience you could not fully make sense of in the past may be leading you back to similar thoughts and feelings today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by making sense of the complex feelings in your inner world, you can draw closer to the heart of a matter that has long occupied you.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you are tracing the source of your repeating thoughts and emotional reactions, but may not yet see all the connections.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to understand what the difficult feelings within you are trying to tell you, facing them without blaming yourself.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to stay patient while circling the same thoughts, and not to let your inner questioning become a fruitless repetition.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your ability to be honest with yourself, to trace the source of your feelings and to draw meaning from complex experiences.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your careful introspection, your patience and your ability to accept, without judging, feelings you have not yet resolved.

Yol.D: In the near future the awareness you develop about a long-repeating thought or emotional reaction may help you make new choices.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by getting to know your own patterns of thought and feeling better, you may discover which matters need deeper reflection.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you understand the complexity of your inner world and make more conscious choices with what you have learned from past experience.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to discover the meaning of your repeating emotional patterns and to approach your own inner truth more patiently.

S5-K3.dAnlam: When the Well of Lost Souls comes upright, a threshold appears where you can notice again a feeling, value or wish from which you believe you have long drifted away. The unseen well behind the mouth of the cave symbolises that what you think you have lost may sometimes only have been forgotten in the depths of your life. You too may reconnect with a side of yourself that once mattered to you but that you gradually set aside. This card does not advise you to return entirely to your old self, but to bring the valuable pieces of your past into your life today. Now you can approach yourself with more understanding and, by noticing the needs you have neglected, strengthen your inner wholeness.
S5-K3.yAnlam: When the Well of Lost Souls comes sideways, the traveller is still standing at the threshold of the cave, listening to the voice rising from the depths of the well without knowing which memory it belongs to. You too may feel that something is missing in your life, while still trying to understand which need, or which value you left behind in the past, this feeling comes from. This card suggests discovering what the feeling of lack is telling you, rather than trying to fill it at once. Sometimes a forgotten interest, a postponed wish or a neglected feeling wants to be remembered again. When you give silence time, the meaning of the call rising from the depths of the well can slowly become clear.
S5-K3.hikaye: In one of the quietest regions of the Duat there was an ancient well hidden beneath dark caves, and in its depths echoed the names, dreams and memories left behind by souls who had forgotten their way. One day a nameless traveller who believed they had lost their own voice reached the threshold of the cave, and from within the well rose a whisper, familiar yet long unheard, calling them back to the traces of their forgotten self. When the traveller looked into the depths of the well, they realised that the darkness was not empty, and that the values, wishes and feelings they had left behind were quietly waiting there. From that day on, the Well of Lost Souls became a sacred underworld sign reminding us that a person can recognise again the pieces of themselves they believed lost, and that sometimes looking into the darkness is necessary to build a new wholeness.
S5-K3.mitDers: Each night Ra passes through the dark caverns of the Duat and is reborn in the morning; the lost piece waits in the darkness, it does not vanish.
S5-K3.mitDikkat: Avoiding the pains of the past and leaving the pieces there.
S5-K3.mitGercek: The ancient Egyptian underworld text known as the Book of Caverns depicts the sun god Ra's passage through the dark regions of the Duat, the beings in those regions and the cosmic journey that leads to rebirth. The account includes dark caverns, scenes associated with Osiris and the different states of existence Ra meets during the night. In the Egyptian Amduat tradition too, Ra's night journey is linked with the cycle of the sun that passes through darkness and appears again in the morning.

Kök.D: An important value or wish you left behind in the past may lie at the root of your search today to feel more whole.
Kök.Y: An emotional need you did not take seriously enough in the past may be the source of a feeling of lack you find hard to explain today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by rediscovering a side of yourself you have long neglected, you can build a stronger bond with your own needs.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to understand what is missing in your inner world and reassessing some wishes you left behind in the past.

Sınav.D: Your trial is not to overlook your present self and needs while recognising again the valuable sides you believe you lost in the past.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to trace the source of the lack within you patiently and without judging yourself, rather than filling it with fear.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is the awareness you have gained from past experience and your ability to recognise forgotten needs again.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to make time for inner silence and to approach feelings you cannot yet name with understanding.

Yol.D: In the near future you may meet a chance to bring back into your life an interest or value you set aside in the past.
Yol.Y: In the near future you may better understand which need is linked to a feeling of lack you have long carried within you.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you integrate the sides of yourself you neglected in the past with your life today, and recognise your own values more clearly.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to discover your forgotten needs and to develop your inner wholeness more consciously.

S5-K4.dAnlam: When the Mask of the Silent Scream comes upright, a threshold appears where you can finally give words to a feeling you have long held inside but struggled to express. The line down the middle of the diamond-shaped mask reminds you that there is a boundary between the strong face you show the world and the real needs of your inner world. You too may notice that you hide some thoughts so as not to upset others, out of fear of being misunderstood, or to appear strong. This card does not advise you to reveal all your feelings to everyone, but to be honest with yourself. Now, by creating a safe space for communication, you can turn the silent scream within you into words that can be understood, and express yourself more genuinely.
S5-K4.yAnlam: When the Mask of the Silent Scream comes sideways, the traveller has not yet opened the mask, but has begun to understand which feeling the voice echoing within comes from. You too may keep repeating in your mind some things you want to say, without yet knowing how or with whom to share them. This card reminds you that you do not have to break your silence at once. Sometimes, to be able to express a feeling, you must first recognise it within yourself. When you weigh what you feel, which boundaries you want to protect and in what conditions you would feel safe, the voice behind the mask can slowly become clear. The time of preparation is part of finding your voice.
S5-K4.hikaye: In the dark halls of the Duat there was a diamond-shaped mask with black stripes that kept the fears, hurts and unspoken words people did not dare to show the world. One day a nameless traveller who believed they always had to appear strong put the mask on their face and felt all their feelings fall silent, while a scream grew within them, echoing between stone walls. A silent guardian met at the passage leading to the presence of Osiris advised the traveller not to break the mask, but to name the feeling hidden beneath it, and when the traveller said for the first time that they were afraid, the line at the centre of the mask parted and let their voice be heard. From that day on, the Mask of the Silent Scream became a sacred underworld sign reminding us that feelings hidden to protect oneself can grow heavier over time, and that true courage is not always appearing strong, but being able to express one's own truth safely.
S5-K4.mitDers: In the presence of Osiris it is not the words spoken that decide, but the heart weighed against the feather of Ma'at; a mask protects, but it does not take the place of truth.
S5-K4.mitDikkat: The compulsion to always appear strong.
S5-K4.mitGercek: Funerary masks used in ancient Egypt were associated with protecting a person's identity and the continuity of their existence in the otherworld; they were made not only to cover the face but to represent an idealised identity and to serve a protective role. Spell 125 of the Book of the Dead, linked with the judgement scene before Osiris, contains the declarations in which the deceased defends their deeds aloud, known in modern scholarship as the Negative Confession; the weighing of the heart against the feather of Ma'at, standing for truth and cosmic order, inspires the relationship between the words spoken outwardly and the truth a person carries.

Kök.D: Being able, later on, to express a feeling you could not voice in the past may have formed the basis of your wish today to be more honest with yourself.
Kök.Y: A thought or feeling you hid in the past in order to appear strong may be affecting the hesitation you feel today in expressing yourself.

Şimdi.D: Right now you can create a space where you can express a need or thought you have long hidden through safe and open communication.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to understand which feelings you hide and why, and need to weigh the right conditions for expressing yourself.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to respect both your own boundaries and the other person's feelings while expressing your true emotions.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to notice which of your feelings are waiting to be expressed, without letting your need for silence become constant self-suppression.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your ability to recognise your feelings, to put your thoughts into words clearly and your courage to communicate honestly with people you trust.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to listen to yourself without judgement and your skill at making sense of your feelings before sharing them.

Yol.D: In the near future, by sharing a thought you have long wanted to express under the right conditions, you may communicate more openly on an important matter.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by better understanding the source of some hidden feelings, you may decide when and how you want to express them.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which, moving away from the compulsion to appear strong, you accept your true feelings and can express them consciously.
Kader.Y: This journey may guide you to recognise the needs you hide behind the mask and towards an inner preparation in which you can develop your own voice with confidence.

S5-K5.dAnlam: When the Sleeping Shadow Serpent comes upright, you may notice that a talent, wish or power to change that you have long kept hidden within you is now ready to move. The serpent coiling between two points symbolises that the road between beginning and outcome is not always straight, and that some powers ripen in silence. You too may have developed the inner resolve to take the first step on something you did not dare to before. This card does not advise you to use your gathered energy without thinking, but to direct it by defining your purpose. Now you can turn your wish for change into a concrete choice and, while respecting your limits, start a new movement in your life.
S5-K5.yAnlam: When the Sleeping Shadow Serpent comes sideways, the ancient serpent has not yet opened its eyes, but it is preparing for the moment of waking as it senses the vibrations around it. You too may be aware of a situation in your life you want to change, yet not have decided which step to take or when to act. This card reminds you not to read your waiting as weakness. For some decisions to grow firm, your wish and the real conditions need to come into harmony. When you observe your desire to move, separate your fears from your needs and weigh your options, you can see more clearly in which direction your hidden power can be used. The serpent's silence is the preparation for awakening.
S5-K5.hikaye: In one of the forgotten passages of the Duat, a black serpent recalling the protective coils of Mehen slept silently around an ancient knot that hid a red spark of life at its centre. While the other beings of the underworld mistook its stillness for weakness, every night the serpent listened to the vibrations of the darkness and learned which gate should open and which power should stay hidden for now. One night, when the balance of the ancient passages shifted, the serpent opened its eyes, but instead of shattering the knots around it, it loosened its coils and let the red light reach a new road. From that day on, the Sleeping Shadow Serpent became a sacred underworld sign reminding us that true power lies not always in acting at once, but in knowing one's own nature, sensing the right time and directing gathered energy consciously.
S5-K5.mitDers: In the same underworld, Mehen protects Ra and Apep threatens him; the serpent's power is neither good nor evil in itself, it depends on how it is directed.
S5-K5.mitDikkat: Using the awakened energy impulsively and without control.
S5-K5.mitGercek: In ancient Egyptian underworld accounts, serpents can stand not only for danger and disorder but also for protection, renewal and the upholding of cosmic order. In the underworld text known as the Amduat, the sun god Ra is encircled during his night journey by the protective serpent god Mehen, which forms the basis of the serpent's hidden and protective power. Apep, by contrast, is the great serpent who threatens Ra's night journey and is associated with cosmic disorder; the opposing roles of the two figures show that the serpent symbol does not in itself mean evil.

Kök.D: Your courage in the past to bring to life a wish you had long kept hidden may have formed the basis of the power to change you have today.
Kök.Y: A decision you postponed in the past, or a talent you did not feel ready to use, may be the source of the potential you are reassessing today.

Şimdi.D: Right now you can create room to move in which you bring an idea you have long been ripening into your life with a conscious step.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you feel the wish for change within you, but may be trying to understand towards which purpose to use this energy.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to direct your awakening power with patience, will and conscious choices, without turning it into hasty reactions.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to judge realistically when you are ready to act, without letting your need for preparation turn into endless postponement.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your inner courage, your determination and your skill at using, under the right conditions, the talents you have long been developing.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your intuitive awareness, your patience and your ability to carefully develop talents that have not yet come to light.

Yol.D: In the near future chances may take shape for you to make concrete a change you have been considering and to make a new beginning by your own will.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by understanding which of your goals is ready to move, you may create firmer conditions for a new beginning.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you know your own power, show courage in the face of change and direct your energy through conscious choices.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to discover your hidden potential, complete your inner preparation and approach more consciously the transformation you will begin by your own will.

S5-K6.dAnlam: When the Moon Mirror of the Underworld comes upright, you can weigh with a more integrated view thoughts, feelings or behaviours about yourself that you have long kept apart. The four half-rings arranged one within another symbolise that the same truth can appear at different depths and from different angles. You too may notice that the traits you find hard to accept are as much a part of your life experience as the sides you see as strengths. This card advises you to look honestly at all your sides without defining yourself by a single identity. Now you can weigh your past choices with your present awareness and strengthen your inner wholeness by treating yourself with more understanding. What the mirror shows is not a fixed verdict but a chance to know yourself more clearly.
S5-K6.yAnlam: When the Moon Mirror of the Underworld comes sideways, the traveller is still standing on the shore of the lake, trying to understand which of the different reflections appearing on the rippling water is their own. You too may find yourself caught between different ideas about yourself as you weigh certain behaviours or emotional reactions. This card reminds you not to accept every reflection you see as a certain truth. Sometimes fears, expectations or past experiences can make you perceive yourself differently from how you are. When you give your feelings time, compare your observations with your real experiences and weigh yourself without judgement, you can notice which reflections are passing and which show your deeper needs.
S5-K6.hikaye: In one of the deepest passages of the Duat there was a dark lake that no star could reach, and on its surface were hidden four separate reflections of a moon not seen in the sky. One day a nameless traveller who wished to escape the dark traces of their own past came to the shore of the lake and saw in the water not a stranger's face, but the faces they themselves had worn at different times throughout their life. At first the traveller wanted to choose one of these images, but the lake's silent keeper told them that all the reflections were born of the same essence, and that the water would grow still only when they could see them all without denying any. From that day on, the Moon Mirror of the Underworld became a sacred underworld sign reminding us that a person can reach a deeper awareness when they accept their bright and shadowed sides as one whole.
S5-K6.mitDers: Thoth measures time by the phases of the moon; in every phase the moon is the same moon. The different faces of the self, too, are phases of a single whole.
S5-K6.mitDikkat: Claiming only the face you like and rejecting what remains in shadow.
S5-K6.mitGercek: In ancient Egypt, Thoth is the god of wisdom, writing and reckoning associated with the moon; his link with the moon's changing phases inspires the idea of an unseen order being understood over time. Khonsu is also an important Egyptian god associated with the moon, linked especially with its cyclical movement. The sun god Ra passing through the Duat during the night and being reborn in the morning also shows that darkness is not only absence but a stage in which transformation takes place.

Kök.D: Understanding a side of yourself you once found hard to accept may have formed the basis for developing a more integrated sense of self today.
Kök.Y: An identity others showed you in the past, or a meaning you gave yourself, may be affecting how you see yourself today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by weighing your strong and vulnerable sides together, you can approach a matter in your life more honestly and in a more balanced way.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be caught between different ideas about yourself and trying to understand which of your feelings reflect your real needs.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to accept the awareness your past choices have given you, without judging them harshly as you face yourself.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to separate your feelings from your observations, without treating passing thoughts about yourself as fixed truths.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your self-awareness, your emotional honesty and your ability to see your different sides as parts of the same whole.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your introspection, the understanding you show yourself and your skill at patiently questioning your own perceptions.

Yol.D: In the near future a new awareness you develop about yourself may help you approach in a more balanced way a situation you have long seen differently.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by reviewing some of your ideas about yourself, you may discover which points of view feel more realistic to you.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you accept your bright and shadowed sides, make peace with past experience and know yourself more wholly.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to tell apart the different reflections of yourself and for a deeper awareness in which you can discover your inner truth without judgement.

S6-K1.dAnlam: When the Gate of the Turning Hourglass comes upright, you may notice that a period in your life is coming to completion and making room for a new stage. The triangle narrowing between two lines symbolises that the experience you have gathered in the past is condensing in your present choices, and that a new point of passage is forming before you. You too may begin to weigh more concretely a change you have long been considering. This card advises you to take the step you are ready for without trying to speed up time. Now you can use what the past has taught you, review the responsibilities you have completed and, by your own will, lay the first stones of a new order of life. The gate takes on meaning when you choose to move forward.
S6-K1.yAnlam: When the Gate of the Turning Hourglass comes sideways, the traveller has not yet turned the hourglass; they are carefully watching the passage that will form between the two chambers of time. You too may sense that a period in your life is about to change, yet not have decided under what conditions you want to move into the new stage. This card reminds you not to read waiting as being unable to move forward. Some passages ask first for an understanding of the responsibilities that must be completed or the decisions that must be clarified. When you weigh your priorities now, you can notice which process is nearing its end and which needs preparation. Though the sand has not yet begun to flow, the conditions of the new cycle are quietly forming.
S6-K1.hikaye: In ancient times, in the shade of the Fusang tree, a mysterious hourglass hung between the end of night and the beginning of morning, and its two chambers linked the roads completed in the past with possibilities not yet opened. One day a nameless traveller who believed they had missed their own time on their celestial journey came before the hourglass and tried to stop the falling grains, but with every interference the glass turned and showed the sign of another passage. At last the traveller stopped trying to control time, watched the gate opening before them, and understood that instead of returning to the past, they could create the start of a new period through their present choice. From that day on, the Gate of the Turning Hourglass became the sacred sign of noticing the right moment of passage instead of trying to change the flow of time, of accepting the periods that have ended, and of stepping consciously into new beginnings.
S6-K1.mitDers: The ten suns rise in turn from the Fusang tree; in the tale of Hou Yi, when all ten rise at once, the world is scorched. Every passage has its order and its time.
S6-K1.mitDikkat: Forcing the passage impatiently before its time has come.
S6-K1.mitGercek: In ancient Chinese mythological accounts, Xihe is described as the consort of the celestial ruler Di Jun and the mother of the ten suns; the suns appearing in the sky in turn, in connection with the sacred tree called Fusang, inspire the orderly progress of the cosmic cycle. In some later accounts Xihe drives the sun's chariot and accompanies the sun on its journey across the sky, strengthening the idea of a celestial figure who guides the movement of time; not all ancient sources, however, describe Xihe as the driver of the sun's chariot. The idea of celestial journey and orderly change in these accounts forms the card's mythological basis.

Kök.D: An important period of life you completed in the past, or a change you made consciously, may have formed the basis of your choices today.
Kök.Y: A passage you postponed in the past while waiting for the right time may be affecting how you approach new beginnings today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by weighing a process that is coming to completion, you can take a conscious and concrete step to move into a new stage.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be observing the conditions of an approaching change and working out which preparations you need to complete before you act.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to make the decisions change requires as you turn towards a new beginning, without overlooking the responsibilities of the past.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to find the balance between preparing and acting, without letting the need to wait for the right time become endless postponement.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is what you have learned from past experience, your skill at judging time and your ability to manage the passages in your life consciously.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your patience, your skill at careful planning and your ability to weigh conditions realistically before starting a new period.

Yol.D: In the near future a responsibility nearing completion, or changing conditions, may create a chance for you to move into a new stage of life.
Yol.Y: In the near future the conditions of the passage you are considering may become clearer, helping you decide which step to take and when.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you can turn past experience into new beginnings and guide the important passages of your life by your own will.
Kader.Y: This journey may lead you to understand the natural flow of time better, to recognise the processes that must be completed and to prepare consciously for new periods.

S6-K2.dAnlam: When the Ring of Eternal Return comes upright, you may notice that a situation you have met before is reappearing in your life under different conditions. The two linked rings symbolise that similar experiences do not always have to produce the same results. You too may see more clearly the difference between how you reacted in the past and the choices you make today. This card advises you to see repeating events not as an unchangeable fate but as chances to put what you have learned into practice. Now you can act differently in a familiar situation and review your old habits consciously. When the cycle begins again, you no longer have to be the old person within it.
S6-K2.yAnlam: When the Ring of Eternal Return comes sideways, the traveller has not yet completed the passage at the centre of the infinity sign; they are trying to understand why the familiar roads before them resemble one another. You too may feel that similar relationships, decisions or situations keep repeating in your life. This card suggests that before trying to change the cycle, you observe the habits and expectations that create it. Sometimes understanding why an experience repeats comes before living it differently. When you compare your past reactions with your present needs, you can notice which behaviours keep bringing you back to the same point and which new options are possible.
S6-K2.hikaye: In the first ages of celestial time, beneath the sacred waters where Changxi bathed her moons, there was hidden a mysterious sign of time made of two linked silver rings, which carried an echo of the past with every turn. One day a nameless traveller who believed they kept repeating the same mistakes began to walk within these rings, and noticed that although they met a familiar gate at every turn, the details around them and their own thoughts were changing. When the traveller, instead of trying to break the ring, discovered at each encounter a meaning they had not seen before, they understood that the same gate now offered them different choices. From that day on, the Ring of Eternal Return became the sign of time reminding us that the experiences that recur in life are not an unchangeable destiny, and that every repetition carries a sacred chance for a person to grow in awareness and give a new response to old patterns.
S6-K2.mitDers: Changxi bathes the twelve moons anew in every cycle; repetition is the rhythm of renewal.
S6-K2.mitDikkat: Treating repetition as fate and not changing the pattern.
S6-K2.mitGercek: The ancient Chinese work Shan Hai Jing, the Classic of Mountains and Seas, tells how Changxi, consort of the celestial ruler Di Jun, gave birth to the twelve moons and bathed them; this account can be linked symbolically with the regular renewal of celestial beings and the repeating rhythms of time. Changxi's twelve moons belong to a separate mythological account from Xihe's ten suns used in card S6-K1. The cycles of sun and moon in Chinese mythology inspire the idea of a celestial order that explains the repeating movements of nature.

Kök.D: What you learned from a repeating experience in the past may have laid the groundwork for approaching similar situations more consciously today.
Kök.Y: A habit or pattern of behaviour you kept up in the past without noticing may be leading you today to look into the meaning of the similar situations you meet.

Şimdi.D: Right now, meeting a situation you have experienced before, you may find a chance to apply what you learned from the past through a different choice.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may feel that certain events in your life keep repeating and be trying to understand which of your habits they are linked to.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to make a new choice in line with what you have learned, without falling back automatically on old reactions in a familiar situation.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to examine patiently the behaviours and expectations that create repeating experiences, without seeing them as unchangeable fate.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your ability to learn from past experience, to recognise similar situations and to develop different behaviour when needed.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your careful observation, your inner awareness and your skill at weighing repeating patterns without judging yourself.

Yol.D: In the near future, when a familiar situation comes up again, you may be able to create a different outcome using what you learned in the past.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by better understanding the source of a repeating habit or way of deciding, you may discover new options for change.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you turn the repetitions in your life into chances for conscious learning and can give new responses to old experiences.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to recognise the patterns of behaviour that stretch from the past to the present and to make more conscious choices in repeating situations.

S6-K3.dAnlam: When Memory Seeping from the Future comes upright, you may notice that a thought about a future not yet lived can give new meaning to your present decisions. The arrow-tipped spiral moving outward symbolises a possibility appearing in your mind and gradually growing clearer. You too may discover a step you can take today as you think about the kind of life you want to build in the future. This card advises you to see your intuitions not as certain prophecies but as signs that help you understand your own expectations. Now you can turn a strong vision of the future into concrete goals and weigh new options in the light of your past experience. What has not yet been lived can inspire your will today.
S6-K3.yAnlam: When Memory Seeping from the Future comes sideways, the traveller is still standing at the centre of the silver spiral, trying to understand what the faint image before them is telling them. You too may carry a strong feeling about your future, a dream that feels familiar, or an expectation you find hard to explain. This card reminds you not to accept the possibilities coming alive in your mind as events that will happen at once. Sometimes the thoughts you form about the future arise from your present needs and past experiences combining in a different way. When you give yourself time, you can tell which images are fed by your desires and which by your worries, and seek a more conscious direction amid uncertainty.
S6-K3.hikaye: In the unseen layers of time, within a mysterious passage recalling the changing seasons of the Ryūgū Palace, there was a silver spiral carrying faint images of moments not yet lived. One day a nameless traveller who worried constantly about their own future felt, at the centre of the spiral, that they recognised a road they had never yet taken, and discovered that the image before them was not a memory left from the past, but a possibility born of their own hopes for the future. Instead of believing the image would certainly come true, the traveller tried to understand which of their desires and fears it was showing them; and so a distant possibility became an awareness that could guide their present choices. From that day on, Memory Seeping from the Future became a sacred sign of time reminding us that a person does not have to know the future in advance, and can shape their present path more consciously by reflecting on possibilities not yet lived.
S6-K3.mitDers: The time Urashima thinks is short corresponds to a very long time in the outer world; the perception of time is relative, and opening the box is a step with no way back.
S6-K3.mitDikkat: Neglecting today's responsibilities while trying to know the future.
S6-K3.mitGercek: In the Japanese legend of Urashima Tarō, the fisherman Urashima helps a sea turtle and is taken to the Ryūgū Palace beneath the sea, where he is welcomed by Princess Otohime. When he returns to land, he learns that far more time has passed in the outer world than the short while he thought he had spent in the palace; the durations and details vary between versions of the story. In some widespread versions the box called tamatebako, given by Otohime, is also linked with the irreversibility of time. This mythological example inspires the theme of time being perceived differently and of a person meeting an age they do not yet know.

Kök.D: A strong dream you formed about your future in the past may have formed the basis of the goals you pursue and the decisions you make today.
Kök.Y: A possibility you wished for in the past but have not yet made sense of may be affecting your expectations of the future today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by seeing more clearly a goal you want to reach in the future, you can arrange your present choices in that direction.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to understand a vague intuition or expectation about your future and need to weigh the possible paths.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to take a conscious step by comparing a strong vision of the future with real conditions, without mistaking it for a certain outcome.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to tell your hopes from your worries, without giving too much meaning to possibilities that have not yet come about.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your ability to think ahead, your creative perspective and your skill at preparing by weighing possible developments.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your ability to observe your intuitions patiently and to stay open to different possibilities while making sense of vague thoughts.

Yol.D: In the near future a new perspective or an inspiring idea may help you set a different path for your long-term goals.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by better understanding the conditions of a possibility you are considering, you may discover which of your expectations need concrete preparation.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you can turn your dreams of the future into conscious choices and approach possibilities not yet realised with creativity.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to make sense of your intuitions and expectations about the future, and to set your own direction more consciously by accepting uncertainty.

S6-K4.dAnlam: When the Broken Mirror of Time comes upright, you may notice that you can give a different meaning to an event from your past than the one you have long seen it through. The three lines parting at the top symbolise that the same moment can carry different feelings and judgements. You too may discover other sides of an experience you once saw as a clear failure, loss or wrong decision. This card does not advise you to try to change the past, but to rethink its meaning in your life today. Now you can review your old judgements, approach yourself more fairly and develop a new view without letting the past limit your present choices more than it should.
S6-K4.yAnlam: When the Broken Mirror of Time comes sideways, the traveller has not yet put the pieces of the mirror together; in each broken surface they watch a different image of the same event. You too may carry differing feelings or judgements about a situation you lived through in the past. This card does not ask you to decide at once which interpretation is certainly right. Sometimes, to grasp the meaning of an event, you need to separate what you knew at the time from what you have learned since. When you give yourself time, weigh the conditions of the past more carefully and make room for other points of view, you can understand which aspects of a memory that seems fragmented are shaping your life today.
S6-K4.hikaye: In a forgotten temple of celestial time there was a mysterious mirror of time, made in the likeness of Amaterasu's sacred mirror, which showed all the moments of the past on a single surface. One day a nameless traveller who believed that a decision they had made in the past had determined their whole life looked into the mirror; the surface split with three fine cracks, and reflections of the same event appeared, carrying different feelings, choices and outcomes. At first the traveller wanted to restore the mirror to its former state, but realising that none of the pieces showed the whole truth on its own, they began to study them side by side. From that day on, the Broken Mirror of Time became a sacred sign of time reminding us that even if what happened in the past cannot be changed, the meanings given to it can be reconsidered, and that sometimes a shattered memory can help us see a wider truth.
S6-K4.mitDers: When Amaterasu withdraws into the cave, the world sinks into darkness; her reflection in the mirror draws her out and the light returns. Truth sometimes becomes visible through a reflection.
S6-K4.mitDikkat: Binding the past to a single, unchangeable verdict.
S6-K4.mitGercek: In the Ame-no-Iwato account recorded in the Japanese Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, the world sinks into darkness when the sun goddess Amaterasu withdraws into a cave, and the other gods seek various ways to bring her out again. The sacred mirror used in this account, Yata no Kagami, plays an important part in Amaterasu's encounter with her own reflection and is linked with the return of light to the world. The mirror is regarded as one of the sacred objects of the Japanese Shinto tradition. This mythological account is the card's main source, in the sense of a hidden truth becoming visible through a reflection and an interrupted order being restored.

Kök.D: Being able to weigh an important event in your past from different sides may have laid the foundation for making more flexible and understanding decisions today.
Kök.Y: Different memories of an event you could not fully make sense of in the past may be leading you today to question your thoughts about that experience again.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by looking from a new angle at a situation you once judged with certainty, you can give your present choices more freedom.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be caught between different thoughts about a past event and trying to understand which interpretation better suits your present needs.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to weigh what happened within its own conditions, without judging your past choices harshly by what you know today.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to accept the aspects of the past that remain unclear, without turning its fragmented memories into a single fixed verdict.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your flexibility of thought, your skill at weighing different points of view and your ability to make new sense of past experiences.
