Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your patient questioning, your power of observation and your ability to examine, without judgement, memories you have not yet made whole.

Yol.D: In the near future, reassessing an event from your past may help you move away from a thought you have long found limiting.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by weighing different information or perspectives about the past, you may grasp more clearly what an event means today.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you do not define your past by a single verdict, weigh your experiences from different sides and shape your present life more freely.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to understand the different reflections of the past and to weigh the events you have lived through with your growing awareness rather than fixed judgements.

S6-K5.dAnlam: When the Shadow of a Forgotten Moment comes upright, you may notice that a small experience you once thought ordinary carries an unexpected meaning for you today. The three separate horizontal lines symbolise that the moments overlooked in the flow of time are not wholly without worth. You too may recall with different feelings an old conversation, a small kindness or an encounter you did not take seriously. This card does not advise you to search the past for some great hidden secret, but to see the value of the small experiences that have shaped your life. Now you can pay closer attention to the details of everyday life and carry into your present choices the awareness that moments you thought unimportant have given you.
S6-K5.yAnlam: When the Shadow of a Forgotten Moment comes sideways, the traveller is still standing between the three lines of time, trying to understand which experiences the faint shadows from the past belong to. You too may sometimes feel that a familiar sound, scent or image awakens in you a feeling you cannot explain. This card reminds you not to assume that behind every feeling there must lie some great hidden event. Some memories show themselves not through clear images but through small associations. When you observe your feelings without forcing them and do not pressure yourself to remember the past completely, you can better understand which small experiences are linked to the values you hold today.
S6-K5.hikaye: On the unseen shore of ancient times there was a silent garden inspired by the tradition of Meng Po's forgetting, and above it hung three silver lines of time that kept the moments people had passed by without noticing. One day a nameless traveller who believed nothing in their life ever changed walked between the lines and saw the shadows of a laugh heard in childhood, a hand held out to them years before and the warmth of an ordinary morning. The traveller realised that none of these moments had been a great event, yet the small traces they had left over time had shaped the values they held today. From that day on, the Shadow of a Forgotten Moment became a sacred sign of time reminding us that time is woven not only from great turning points, but also from small moments that pass unnoticed and quietly add meaning to a person's life.
S6-K5.mitDers: In folk belief, Meng Po's drink makes the soul forget its past life so that a new one can begin; forgetting and remembering are both part of the journey.
S6-K5.mitDikkat: Over-reading small signs, or dismissing everyday moments as worthless.
S6-K5.mitGercek: In later Chinese folk belief, Meng Po is described as the figure who, at the end of the journey through the otherworld, offers souls a drink that makes them forget their past lives. This tradition, associated with the Naihe Bridge and the drink of forgetting, inspires the symbolic relationship between remembering the past and leaving it behind. The Meng Po narrative is a tradition that developed over time, blending Chinese folk religion with Buddhist and Taoist influences; it is not a fixed part of early Chinese mythology.

Kök.D: A small experience you once thought unimportant may have played a more meaningful part than you think in forming a value or behaviour you have today.
Kök.Y: The emotional trace left by a moment you did not pay enough attention to in the past may be the source of a familiar feeling you find hard to explain today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, thanks to a small detail you remember from the past, you may notice again an important value you have overlooked in daily life.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be exploring the meaning of a familiar feeling or association and observing how small experiences from the past are reflected in your life today.

Sınav.D: Your trial is not to overlook the values and insights small experiences have given you while focusing on the big events of your life.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to observe patiently the feelings that vague emotional traces from the past awaken in you, without trying to force an explanation.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is the attention you give to small details, your ability to notice the precious moments of the past and to draw meaning from everyday experience.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your emotional sensitivity, your patience and your skill at observing, without judging yourself, associations you have not yet made sense of.

Yol.D: In the near future a small detail of an old memory, or an everyday encounter, may help you notice again an important value in your life.
Yol.Y: In the near future a familiar feeling or small association may prompt you to explore the link between your past experiences and your present thoughts.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you understand that your life is not made only of great turning points and consciously cherish the value of small moments.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to notice the quiet traces of the past, to explore the meaning of everyday experience and to approach the small details of your life with more sensitivity.

S6-K6.dAnlam: When the Knotted Thread of Time comes upright, you can see more clearly how the decisions you made, the relationships you formed or the responsibilities you took on in the past are bound together today. The three lines meeting at a common point symbolise that developments you thought independent of one another can affect the same matter in your life. You too may reassess which bonds you want to keep in a matter where you are caught between different expectations. This card does not advise you to cut all the ties you formed in the past, but to decide what they mean today. Now, through open communication, conscious choice and mutual understanding, you can bring order to a situation that seems tangled and give your future a more balanced direction.
S6-K6.yAnlam: When the Knotted Thread of Time comes sideways, the traveller is still standing before the sacred knot, trying to understand from which times the tangled threads have come. You too may need to draw connections between the promises you made in the past, your present needs and your expectations of the future. This card reminds you that you do not have to untangle every relationship or responsibility that seems complicated at once. Sometimes the first step to loosening a knot is noticing which thread belongs to you and which to the expectations of others. When you weigh your bonds carefully, you can understand more clearly which responsibilities should continue and which need to be talked through again.
S6-K6.hikaye: In a mysterious celestial garden where moonlight touched every age of time at once, there was a sacred three-stranded knot, inspired by Yue Lao's red threads of fate, binding together the promises of the past, the choices of the present and the possibilities of the future. One day a nameless traveller who felt trapped between old promises and new goals in life came before the knot and pulled the threads hard, but with every pull noticed how roads that seemed far apart met at the same centre. When at last, instead of trying to cut the threads, the traveller told apart which bond was responsibility, which was habit and which was a choice freely kept, the knot loosened and a new road opened before them. From that day on, the Knotted Thread of Time became a sacred sign of time reminding us that the bonds between past and future can shape a person's life, but that understanding the meaning of these bonds and choosing how to respond to them is an important part of personal maturity.
S6-K6.mitDers: In the folk tale, the red thread Yue Lao ties can stretch and tangle but it does not break; bonds can knot, and untying them takes patience.
S6-K6.mitDikkat: Losing your own boundaries through a fatalistic attachment.
S6-K6.mitGercek: In Chinese tradition, Yue Lao, the Old Man Under the Moon, is the mythological figure associated with marriage and matchmaking, believed to create the bonds of fate between people with red threads. In the Dinghun Dian (the Inn Where Marriages Are Settled) story dating back to the Tang dynasty, an old figure whom a young man named Wei Gu meets in the moonlight explains that the feet of those who will marry are tied together by invisible red threads. This tradition inspires the idea of relationships that reach beyond time and distance.

Kök.D: An important decision you made or a relationship you formed in the past may have laid the groundwork for seeking balance between different responsibilities today.
Kök.Y: A promise or mutual expectation that was never fully clarified in the past may be the source of the relational complexity you are trying to untangle today.

Şimdi.D: Right now, by weighing together the different responsibilities that stretch from the past to the present, you can make more balanced choices in a complicated matter in your life.
Şimdi.Y: Right now you may be trying to understand how different relationships and expectations affect one another, and weighing which bonds to give priority to.

Sınav.D: Your trial is to make balanced decisions that respect the bonds you formed in the past while also protecting your present needs and personal boundaries.
Sınav.Y: Your trial is to tell which of the tangled responsibilities truly belong to you, without rushing to untangle them.

Yardımcı.D: The force that supports you is your ability to understand the mutual expectations in your relationships, to communicate openly and to find ways of reconciliation in complicated situations.
Yardımcı.Y: The force that supports you is your patient judgement, your ability to listen to different points of view and to examine carefully bonds that have not yet become clear.

Yol.D: In the near future, by rearranging a responsibility or relationship that comes from the past, you may create a healthier balance between your different goals in life.
Yol.Y: In the near future, by better understanding the source of some responsibilities that seem bound together, you may decide in which matters clarity or a frank conversation is needed.

Kader.D: This journey may carry you to a maturity in which you weigh consciously the bonds you formed in the past, balance mutual responsibilities and steer your own future through freer choices.
Kader.Y: This journey may prepare you to discover the meaning of relationships and responsibilities formed at different times and to decide more consciously which bonds you want to keep.

S1.cerceve: In Aztec cosmology the universe is ordered around four directions and a centre; the sky has thirteen layers and the underworld nine. The world has passed through five ages of the sun, and the present age is the Fifth Sun (Nahui Ollin). According to the Teotihuacan account, this sun was born when Nanahuatzin gave himself to the fire, yet it began to move only with the help of the other gods. Order does not sustain itself; it is kept through movement, devotion and reciprocity.

S2.cerceve: Greek mythology portrays the human being as standing between the gods and fate, responsible for their own choices. The Delphic maxim "Know thyself", the idea that excess (hubris) meets its due, and the hero's journey home (nostos) are the basic patterns of this world. The set name Prometheion refers to Prometheus, the titan who took fire from the gods and gave it to humankind.

S3.cerceve: In the Norse accounts (Völuspá, Gylfaginning), the universe begins in the primordial void called Ginnungagap, where the ice of Niflheim meets the fire of Muspelheim. The nine worlds rest upon the tree Yggdrasil; fate is set by the Norns, and even the gods are subject to it. Ragnarök is a great destruction, but according to the Völuspá the world grows green again afterwards.

S4.cerceve: This set is inspired by the Dreaming traditions of Aboriginal Australian peoples, known by names such as Jukurrpa and Tjukurpa. These traditions are not one shared mythology; they differ by community, language and land. A common thread is that the journeys of ancestral beings shaped the earth, that knowledge is passed on through songs and travelling routes (songlines), and that the concept of Country expresses the mutual responsibility between people, ancestors and land.

S5.cerceve: In Egyptian belief the sun god Ra passes each night through the otherworld called the Duat and is reborn in the morning. The Amduat, the Book of Gates and the Book of Caverns describe the hours, gates and dangers of this journey. Apep, the serpent who threatens order, and Mehen, the protecting serpent, face each other on the same journey. In spell 125 of the Book of the Dead, the heart is weighed against the feather of Ma'at, who stands for truth and cosmic order.

S6.cerceve: This set draws on Chinese and Japanese narratives; the set name Samsarion refers to saṃsāra, the cycle of birth, death and rebirth in Indian and Buddhist thought. In Chinese accounts, Xihe's ten suns rise in turn from the Fusang tree, Changxi bathes the twelve moons, Meng Po makes souls forget the past, and Yue Lao binds people together with red threads. In Japanese accounts, Urashima Tarō meets the relativity of time, and Amaterasu meets her own reflection in the mirror.

motifler.isik: The loss and return of light
